new_hire_deadline_text: not later than 90 days after their hire date
provider_approval_type: approved training provider by the Office of the Attorney General (OAG)
enforcing_agencies: local, state, and federal law enforcement
applicable_to: commercial lodging establishments with 10 or more rooms
required_topics: how and why human trafficking occurs within the hospitality industry
roles and responsibilities of employees in reporting and responding to human trafficking
identification of signs and indicators of human trafficking among individuals working in commercial lodging
contact information for appropriate entities to report human trafficking
recordkeeping_requirements: maintain records showing compliance with Section 114.0051 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code
records must be available for review and inspection by the OAG, as well as local, state, and federal law enforcement
certificate_requirements: a certificate of completion from an approved training provider
law_references: Section 114.0051 of the Texas Business and Commerce Code
risks_or_constraints: establishments must provide annual training, which can be expensive if not using an approved provider
recordkeeping and certification requirements add administrative burden
notes: The OAG maintains a list of approved human trafficking training videos.
Training providers may charge for their courses.
